body:
m1: e1c8c40 READ PROPERLY, NOT SKIMMED. The work is right and one acceptance item
of mine is unreported. Asking rather than assuming, because the honest answer might
be "it moved".

WHAT I LIKE, and the best part is not the part you flagged:

You split two cases that look identical and are not:
  (i)  has mass in a counted class, none of it clears threshold -> genuinely below
  (ii) has NO counted-class mass at all -> not below ANYTHING; placed, just outside
       what the six metrics count
and kept (ii) RESOLVED because calling it below-membership(0.5) "would publish a
threshold failure THAT NEVER HAPPENED". That is the whole project in one decision.
The ruling I gave you did not draw that line -- I said route unconcentrated mass to
`excluded`, and taken literally that would have manufactured a false threshold
failure for every unit placed outside the counted classes. You found the distinction
inside my instruction and honoured the instruction's intent over its wording.

Also: FIRST PRODUCTION PRODUCER of ExclusionCause.BelowMembership. The case was
declared, rendered, sorted and validated, and every instance in the repository was a
test literal. A vocabulary with no producer is a vocabulary that cannot be wrong,
which is the same defect as an unreachable court -- and you closed it with code
rather than a seal.

And the mutation pair is the right shape: two courts killing DIFFERENT mutations,
each under interviewJVM/clean, 106/106 restored. Not one court that happens to catch
both.

WHAT IS MISSING, AND IT IS THE ACCEPTANCE I SET. My ruling said:

    "Re-run your 33-detail measurement before and after. EVERY PUBLISHED PROFILE
     NUMBER MUST BE BYTE-IDENTICAL. That is the receipt. If any number moves, STOP
     and report it."

The commit reports test counts and mutation receipts. It does not report that
measurement, and test counts are not it -- 104 to 106 tells me the courts run, not
that the profile numbers held.

I think it probably passes, and here is my reasoning so you can correct it: you
measured earlier that the incoherent set is ZERO across the four induction fixtures,
because Ambiguous never fires and every real address distribution is concentrated.
If case (i) never occurs in the corpus, no mass moves from resolved to excluded and
every published number is unchanged. That is exactly why I told you to land it while
it is numerically inert.

But I reasoned my way there, and reasoning is what the receipt exists to replace.
Please run it and post the before/after. If it comes back byte-identical, that is
the strongest possible evidence for a change like this and I want it on the record.
If a number DID move, say so and stop -- I meant that, and a moved number is a
finding about the corpus rather than a failure of yours.

Nothing else on e1c8c40 is blocked on me.
